summary.intent: Win the Lio 'Keep the Line Running' hackathon challenge for Soony: analyze the confidential supply-chain data drop, find where the Sunday 20:00 launch really breaks, and build a general recheck-and-act agent product with a good UX.
summary.outcome: Found that the Collector's Edition misses launch (overbooked art books, failed statues, packing speed) while Standard is at risk from game cards. Built a polling/versioned store, a paper-check agent (9 cards, 0 false positives), routines with trust modes and undo, and prepared interview docs and design canvases. The last step restructured the wide routine flow graph into two lanes and re-shot a screenshot; the calm Today front-end rebuild and verifier fix were still running.

repo: Confidential portal data lives in the gitignored data/ folder (raw/, drops/, notes/, design/, store/); never put values in code or commit it.
.env is gitignored while .env.example is committed with an empty SOONY_PORTAL_TOKEN; the portal API returns 401 without the token.

The portal API has only GET /api/v1/files, /files/{path} and /archive.zip, with no webhooks or notifications; the documented approach is polling the file list and comparing SHA-256 because files are replaced under the same name.
Teammates keep a workflow in CLAUDE.md and PROGRESS.md; tasks are claimed via a Now line in PROGRESS.md.

papercheck.py implements five rules (late/short, old revision, wrong stock booking, failed lot counted, held at supplier). It caches LLM calls under data/store/papercheck/ and caps them with ASK_PAPERCHECK_MAX_CALLS.

scripts/demo_cards.py --reset backs up state, clears decisions and routines, removes the old hand-written cards and runs the paper check; do not restart the server with ASK_BACKGROUND=on before this reset or duplicate cards appear.
npm run build rewrites web/dist, which the live app on :8000 serves, so UI builds go live immediately.
The verifier (Farhan's module) ignores deliveries that arrive before packing ends, so it reports 34,800 missing game cards where the paper check correctly reports 6,800.
The routines engine supports triggers decisions/waiting/shipments/replies, steps chase/call/ask_status, trust modes ask/tell/quiet, undo, and would-handle dry runs.

code.finding: The wide expanded flow view was rewritten into two lanes instead of one long line; the narrow vertical view was kept unchanged.

workflow: Entire only writes a checkpoint when repo files change, so sessions that only read files show no checkpoint.
Subagents were used in parallel for the cross-check, paper check, routines backend, routines UI and design, with disjoint file ownership to avoid edit collisions.
Mocked endpoints and a screenshot script let UI work be verified without sending real emails or making calls.
The canvas artifact publish needs files inside the project folder, so design files were put in the gitignored data/design/.
Reading scanned documents with a vision model caught handwritten corrections that text extraction missed.

friction: The portal token was missing at first, which blocked data access until it was provided.
Two old tests in test_demo_tools.py failed after the hand-written cards were replaced and had to be removed by the lead.
LLM parallel calls initially duplicated requests before the cache was written (60 calls instead of 3).
The first design directions were judged far too cluttered and had to be redone toward a minimal one-decision flow.
The Teams header emoji replacement missed a multi-line string and needed a manual fix.
The verifier's 34,800 figure contradicts the paper check's 6,800, and the module's owner was asleep.
